quiz.q: When is the Remove Variable component most useful, per the lecture?
options: At the very end of every flow
Mid-flow, to free memory held by a big variable (e.g. a large saved payload) that's no longer needed
To remove headers from the request
quiz.explain: Removing a variable frees its memory. At the end of a flow it isn't needed since everything is cleared anyway; small variables don't matter much.

quiz.q: The POST implementation now returns transactionId and employeeId, which aren't in the RAML. What should you do?
options: Nothing — the RAML is only documentation
Update the response example and data type in Design Center, publish a new version, and update Studio
Edit the read-only spec inside src/main/resources/api
Remove the fields from the response
quiz.explain: Keep spec and implementation consistent: a new team member checks the RAML first and may give consumers the wrong structure.

quiz.q: You published spec 1.0.1. What happens in Studio automatically?
options: Nothing — update via Manage dependencies or edit the version in pom.xml
Studio re-scaffolds and overwrites all flows
quiz.explain: Studio isn't updated automatically. Re-scaffolding doesn't overwrite implemented flows either — only empty flows for new resources are generated.

quiz.q: After bumping the dependency to 1.0.1 in pom.xml, requests fail with "Raml not found". What else must be changed?
options: The APIkit router configuration's API definition, which still references version 1.0.0
quiz.explain: The router's API definition included the version, so it searched for 1.0.0. Update both the dependency and the router config.

quiz.q: In the PATCH input parameters { emp_salary: payload.empSalary, … }, what is on the left side?
options: Keys — placeholders named like the table columns
quiz.explain: Left = keys/placeholders named like DB columns; right = values from our payload or variables.

quiz.q: A PATCH for a non-existent employee ID runs without error. What does the Update return?
quiz.explain: No error is raised, but nothing was updated, so the class added a check on affectedRows.

quiz.q: How did the class make PATCH fail when no row is updated?
options: Is number on payload.affectedRows with min 1 and max 1
A Try scope with On Error Continue
quiz.explain: If affectedRows isn't exactly 1, Is number raises VALIDATION:INVALID_NUMBER. A Choice with Raise Error (or Is false) would also work.

quiz.q: You map VALIDATION:INVALID_NUMBER to DATABASE:NO_DATA_FOUND on the Is number component. Which handler type must match it now?
quiz.explain: After error mapping, the handler must match the custom type, not the original — also a certification-style question.

quiz.q: What does a Database Select return when one row matches?
options: An array of objects (Java) with one element — access it with payload[0]
quiz.explain: A Select can return many rows, so it's always an array of objects, one per row; output application/json converts it to JSON.

quiz.q: GET /api/employees/1000 returns 200 with every field null except active. The mapping used payload[0].empId, payload[0].empName… What's the bug?
options: The right side must use the DB column names, e.g. payload[0].emp_id
quiz.explain: Left side = response fields per the contract; right side = DB values with column names.

quiz.q: For GET of a non-existent employee, what did the class decide to return?
options: 200 with a message like "employee details not found in the database", via Choice on !isEmpty(payload)
quiz.explain: The team chose success with a not-found message for GET. isEmpty is preferred over sizeOf for large/streamed data.

quiz.q: mvn clean package fails with "Global element 'error-handler' does not provide a name attribute". What's the cause?
options: The error handler has no ANY handler
A top-level error-handler has no name — every global error handler needs one so flows can reference it
quiz.explain: In the student's file a second top-level error-handler lacked a name; give it a name or merge it into the named handler.

cards.back: Deletes a variable by name to free memory — useful for large variables no longer needed mid-flow.
Allowed, e.g. status `'active'` on insert since all new employees are active. Keep others as input parameters for neatness.

cards.front: Response structure changed — what else must change?
cards.back: RAML example + data type in Design Center → publish new version → update Studio dependency → update router API definition if it has the version.

cards.front: Why keep RAML and implementation in sync?
cards.back: APIs are permanent, people change: a new member reads the RAML first and could give consumers the wrong structure.

cards.front: Updating the spec dependency in Studio
cards.back: Right-click project → **Manage dependencies** → Update version; or edit the version in **pom.xml**.
APIkit config pointing to the spec; may include the version, e.g. `…:hr-employees-sapi-7303:1.0.0:raml:zip:…`.
No. Only empty flows for new resources are generated; existing flows remain.
Left = keys (placeholders named like table columns). Right = values from payload or variables.
Rows changed by Update/Insert. `0` on PATCH means the employee didn't exist.
Validates values: Is number, Is email, IP, URL, null, empty/blank, empty collection, true/false, …
Value `#[payload.affectedRows]`, type INTEGER, min 1, max 1. Otherwise raises `VALIDATION:INVALID_NUMBER`.
Converts a component's error type into a custom one, e.g. `VALIDATION:INVALID_NUMBER` → `DATABASE:NO_DATA_FOUND`.
`NAMESPACE:IDENTIFIER`, like `HTTP:CONNECTIVITY` or `DATABASE:NO_DATA_FOUND`.

cards.front: Why did deployment fail with a custom error type in a handler?
cards.back: No component raised or mapped that type; Mule validates referenced error types at deployment.
A Choice (`payload.affectedRows == 0`) with Raise Error, or Validation **Is false**.

cards.front: What does a Database Select return?
cards.back: An **array of objects** (Java), one per row — even for one row. Access with `payload[0]`.
Left = response fields per the contract; right = DB column values, e.g. `empId: payload[0].emp_id`.

cards.front: Should "record not found" be an error?
cards.back: Depends on the agreed design. Here GET returns **200** with "employee details not found in the database".
`isEmpty` checks existence; `sizeOf` counts. `isEmpty` is preferred for large/streamed data.
One query per operation; for several use **Execute Script** or a **stored procedure**.
The debugger port — the app was already running; stop it before debugging again.
A `name` attribute, so flows can reference it; otherwise the build fails.
